literal: Ruin and increase non-existent are not; of the mind unbending to the noble ones is ornament.
translation: Loss and gain are not uncommon in life. To remain unbending in mind through them is the true ornament of the noble.
modern: வாழ்வில் அழிவும் பெருக்கமும் இல்லாதவை அல்ல, அவை இயற்கையே. ஆனால் அந்த நிலைகளிலும் மனம் கோணாமல் நடுநிலையோடு இருப்பதே சான்றோர்களுக்கு அழகாகும்.
explanation: This couplet observes that loss and gain are inevitable parts of human life. The phrase 'il alla' emphasizes that these fluctuations are not non-existent, meaning they happen to everyone. The true mark of nobility, therefore, is 'kōṭāmai'—the unbending impartiality of the mind. Maintaining this steady, unbiased state regardless of changing fortunes is described as the greatest ornament for the wise.
